claim: Spontaneous per-step explaining separates good from poor learners of worked examples (Chi 1989: 4 vs 4 students, 82% vs 46% correct; about 15 vs 3 explanations per example), but this is a post-hoc correlation with N=8 and the original paper was only read second-hand.
agent_test: Compare agent runs that write a one-line cause per step with runs that only read the step, at equal tokens; check whether per-step explanation count predicts final accuracy.

claim: Prompting students to self-explain beats unprompted study in a small experiment (Chi 1994: gain 32% vs 22%, N=14 vs 10; hard questions +22.6 vs +12.5), but prompted students spent about twice as long (2h05 vs 1h06).
agent_test: Run explain-prompt vs no-prompt with tokens equalised by giving the control extra passes or samples.

claim: Inducing self-explanation has a medium pooled effect, g=.55 (69 effect sizes, 64 reports, N=5,917, I2=65%), with large heterogeneity; a fail-safe N of 6,028 argues against pure publication bias.
agent_test: Use g about .5 as the prior; expect shrinkage once time or compute is matched.

claim: The effect is largest against no-explanation controls (g=.67, k=41) and much smaller against instructional explanation (g=.35, k=6) or another strategy (g=.30, k=7). Part of the effect is therefore extra processing, not explaining specifically.
agent_test: The control arm must get equal extra tokens spent on something else (extra samples, restating the step), not a bare baseline.

claim: When time is matched, the self-explanation advantage often vanishes: McEldoon 2013 found little difference from extra problems, Scheitz 2025 (N=238) found no added benefit over extra practice, and Chen 2026 found equal gains with 3.5x fewer problems. Gap search: McEldoon 2013 (N=69) found the edge over time-matched practice small and only on some subscales; Matthews and Rittle-Johnson 2009 (n=48) found no effect of prompts after conceptual instruction.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison against best-of-N / more attempts is the decisive test; do not credit the effect without it.

claim: Conceptual and generic prompts work; metacognitive prompts (g=.19, ns) and multiple-choice prompt format (g=.24, ns) do not. Prompt content matters.
agent_test: Make the S5 slot ask what is wrong and why the step follows, not whether it is understood; compare against a confidence-style prompt.

claim: Learners are poor monitors: poor solvers said they understood 85% of the time, and 'everything is clear' appeared three times more in poor protocols. Bare 'I understand' monitoring fails; explaining exposes gaps.
agent_test: Compare an agent's self-rated 'step is fine' against an explicit explanation slot that must name the justifying rule.

claim: About a quarter of human self-explanations are wrong, yet gains held when they were partialed out. Feedback after explaining helps near transfer (N=94, 90.7 vs 82.0) but not far transfer.
agent_test: Test whether an agent that explains with a known-wrong explanation still improves; add an external check after the explanation.

claim: The benefit lies in integrating text with prior knowledge (at least 30% of explanations); transfer on ill-defined problems is mediated by explanation quality, more so for low-aptitude learners.
agent_test: Score explanation quality, not count, as the predictor of agent success.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Open-ended LLM-feedback self-explanation improved transfer explanation quality (+11.9 points, d=0.44, N=92) while menu-based did not (+4.7, ns); total post-test score did not differ.
agent_test: Free-text one-line error naming versus a fixed menu of error types in the agent.

claim: Grading explanations with an LLM is only moderately reliable: GPT-5.1 vs humans weighted kappa .66-.78, tutor correctness kappa .32 with more false negatives (42) than false positives (16), and LLMs falsely flagged 27% of correct code explanations.
agent_test: Do not let the same model grade its own explanation; use a separate verifier and measure false-flag rate.

claim: Self-explanation prompting helps LLMs on some tasks: dialogue understanding (MultiWOZ JGA 35.93 to 44.44; STARv2 51.88 to 63.66) where chain-of-thought did not help (27.64), and knowledge reasoning (MedMCQA 56.6 vs human CoT 53.2).
agent_test: Run explain-each-step vs CoT vs plain at equal tokens on a held-out set.

claim: LLM explanation gains depend on model scale and explanation reliability: small models do not benefit (Lampinen), explanations can be unfaithful (Turpin, Lanham), and gains shrink for stronger models (Spider +2.8 Codex vs +0.4 GPT-4). A factuality check lifted SYNTH from 52.4% to 74.8%.
agent_test: Check gain by model strength; add a factuality check on the explanation.

claim: Explanations generated with the right answer given are only slightly better than with a wrong answer (56.6 vs 56.0 MedMCQA), so for in-context exemplars the correctness of the explanation matters little. Wang 2023: invalid-reasoning demonstrations keep 81 percent of CoT on GSM8K (39.5 vs 48.5), while removing relevance drops it to 11.0.
agent_test: Replace the explanation with a plausible wrong one of equal length and compare.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback often hurts reasoning (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0). Self-explanation must be paired with an external signal.
agent_test: Compare explain-and-revise with and without an executable or oracle check.

claim: Explanation plus execution feedback adds small gains: Self-Debug +2.8 on Spider for Codex (81.3 to 84.1) and +0.9 on TransCoder over unit tests (91.6 to 92.5), while a trace hurt (87.9). Reflexion self-reflection added about +8 on HotPotQA over episodic memory alone, but self-reflection without tests lowered Rust results (0.52 vs 0.60).
agent_test: Test one-line error naming as the reflection written to memory, with and without a test.

claim: Self-explanation as a training signal works: ExP-GRPO reaches MATH level-5 pass@4 of 23% vs 12% (GRPO with expert CoT) on a 3B model, and STaR rationalization lifts CommonsenseQA 68.8 to 72.5.
agent_test: Training-based; outside scaffold scope, note only.

claim: The unit of explanation matters: 'explain every utterance' (44.44) beat 'first summarize' (40.98) and 'first understand' (36.52) on MultiWOZ.
agent_test: Per-step explanation vs one upfront summary at equal tokens.

claim: The pooled effect is heavily moderated (East Asia g=1.19 vs North America .53; more-time studies .72 vs .41, ns); a single pooled number is not a safe prior.
agent_test: Report effect by task family, not pooled.

claim: Alternatives can match or beat self-explanation: hypothetico-deduction teaching beat it for clinical reasoning (accuracy .22 vs .17, N=88), and in a 2026 medical study self-explanation beat example-based teaching only at day 10, not day 40.
agent_test: Compare explain-step against structured hypothesis testing in the agent's diagnostic tasks.

claim: No published test was found that implements the Chi 1989 mechanism (explain each example step) as a scaffold on an LLM and measures it at equal tokens.
agent_test: This is our experiment: S5 one-line naming vs none vs extra sample at equal tokens.

claim: At fixed compute the best use depends on difficulty: sequential revision wins on easy items, parallel sampling or verifier search on hard ones (Snell 2024, PaLM 2-S*, MATH; about 4x efficiency gain from allocating by difficulty). So S5 (sequential explain-and-revise) is not a universal use of equal tokens.
agent_test: Route by estimated difficulty: S5 revise on medium items, extra samples on hard items; measure at equal tokens.

claim: Content of the explanation matters less than its relevance and order: invalid-reasoning demonstrations keep 81 percent of CoT on GSM8K (39.5 vs 48.5), while irrelevant ones fall to 11.0, below standard prompting (15.4). Error-naming is not shown to be special for generation.
agent_test: Test wrong-but-plausible explanation arm; do not claim that correctness of the line is what drives gains.

claim: What helps in the correct-and-revise loop is locating the error: LLMs find reasoning mistakes poorly (GPT-4 52.87 on BIG-Bench Mistake) but fix them well when told the step; self-feedback gave 0 gain on math because the model replied everything looks good in 94 percent of cases; specific feedback beat generic (27.5 vs 26.0 vs 24.8 on code optimization).
agent_test: S5 line must name a specific step and fault; gate revision on an external check or a >65 percent reliable error-finder.

claim: Self-grading is biased: LLM judges recognize their own output and favor it, with preference rising linearly with self-recognition (Panickssery 2024); GPT-4 judge agrees with humans over 80 percent but has position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias (Zheng 2023).
agent_test: Score explanations with a different model, randomised order, or an executable check; never the generator alone.

claim: Step-level checking beats outcome checking on long chains: PRM 78.2 vs ORM 72.4 vs majority vote 69.6 (best-of-1860, MATH); CoT gains concentrate in symbolic (14.2), math (12.3) and logic (6.9) tasks, near zero elsewhere (0.7).
agent_test: Apply per-step explanation on formal multi-step tasks; skip it for knowledge or open tasks.

claim: Primary Chi 1989 and Chi 1994 texts and Schworm and Renkl 2006 could not be opened (HTTP 403, login redirect, API rate limits); their numbers stay second-hand.
agent_test: Do not cite the exact Chi numbers as verified.
